# llms.txt

> A plain-text summary of Vraj Patel's professional portfolio.

## Identity
- **Name:** Vraj Patel
- **Positioning:** Systems Integration Engineer
- **Location:** Boulder, Colorado
- **Focus:** Systems integration, backend/platform engineering, automation, data engineering, and applied-ML infrastructure

## Education
- **Dual M.S. programs:** Computer Science and Engineering Management, University of Colorado Boulder
- **B.S. in Computer Science, Business Minor:** University of Colorado Boulder

## Professional Summary
Vraj Patel turns operational friction into reliable software and data systems. At CU Boulder, he builds internal backend services, operational analytics, automation, and human-reviewed ML workflows. His research background includes public-interest data systems and satellite cybersecurity.

## Professional Experience

### University of Colorado Boulder · Institute of Behavioral Science
**Systems Integration Engineer (May 2025–present)**
- Building an internal FastAPI, React/TypeScript, and PostgreSQL support-operations platform around a current 10,803-ticket Freshdesk-backed corpus, with support-group IDs recorded for 96.7% of records.
- Developed and evaluated an unreleased BERT routing candidate on 6,137 training tickets, reaching 82.63% sealed-test accuracy and 0.7563 macro-F1.
- Built a React, Vite, and Recharts dashboard that separates source intake from reportable volume and exposes busiest weekdays and peak hours independently.
- Reduced the analytics visualization payload by 61% raw and 66% gzip by replacing Plotly with Recharts and accessible chart tables.
- Built a PowerShell offboarding tool that reduced a typical group-membership cleanup from about 15 minutes to under one minute.

### University of Colorado Boulder · Institute of Behavioral Science
**Lead Technical Research Assistant (March 2023–May 2025)**
- Held a separate, concurrent IBS appointment with independent visual-bias and legislative-data workstreams.
- Built PyTorch and ResNet50 workflows for visual-bias research using New York Times COVID-19 imagery.
- Built checkpointed Selenium, BeautifulSoup, and LegiScan pipelines for 15+ years of legislative data, reducing redundant bulk-ingestion requests by approximately 40%.

### Studio Lab · University of Colorado Boulder
**Research Assistant, Data Engineering and ML (January 21–April 13, 2024)**
- Held a paid CU Boulder appointment for the evaluation phase of the Indian parliamentary-data project.
- Continued collaborating on the research after the Studio Lab appointment ended; that collaboration was not an extension of the Studio Lab payroll appointment.
- Designed WER-oriented comparisons across Deepgram, Google Speech-to-Text, Amazon Transcribe, and Azure Speech.
- Set up translation comparisons across Google Cloud Translation, Amazon Translate, and Azure Translator to determine workflow fit.

### Princeton University
**Research Assistant — Indian Parliamentary Data, functional title (January 15, 2025–May 2026)**
- Paid directly by Princeton under a separate appointment to continue the Studio Lab project.
- Built the scraping logic and orchestrated collection, speech and translation processing, PDF text extraction, normalization, and structured outputs end to end.
- Processed 40+ GB of campaign audio and thousands of parliamentary documents with restartable state and reviewable intermediate artifacts.

### The Data Mine of the Rockies · Purdue University and L3Harris
**Undergraduate Research Assistant, Satellite Telemetry Data Analysis (August 2024–May 2025)**
- Worked directly with L3Harris senior engineers through Purdue's Data Mine of the Rockies.
- Trained anomaly-detection models on synthetic satellite telemetry and mapped space-cyber scenarios to SPARTA and MITRE ATT&CK.
- Co-authored and presented “L3Harris: Satellite Cyberattack Detection” at the inaugural Data Mine of the Rockies Symposium in Colorado Springs.
- Spring 2025 research poster: https://datamine.purdue.edu/posters/1-DMR_S25_Poster_L3_48-x-36-1.pdf

## Research Writing

## Selected Work

### Operational Ticket Intelligence
- **Domain:** Software Engineering
- **Tech:** FastAPI, PostgreSQL, React, TypeScript, SQLAlchemy, Recharts, scikit-learn, Docker
- Full-stack support operations joining dependable backend workflows, lifecycle-aware analytics, and advisory support-group routing suggestions.
- Separates offline training and candidate packaging from serving while keeping interactive predictions advisory and auditable.
- Validated a historical 10,399-ticket canonical rebuild with 35,001 conversations and 1,525 attachment-metadata rows.
- Verified a current local database of 10,803 tickets on August 27, 2026; 96.7% carried nonblank support-group IDs. Fourteen IDs were observed, but 13 mapped to the current runtime configuration and one legacy unmapped ID appeared on three records.
- Applied lifecycle, provenance, text-quality, group-policy, and minimum-support gates to produce a current 6,487-record, seven-class training-eligible corpus.
- Measured 524 newly created tickets and 610 records with source update timestamps in the preceding 30 days. These are overlapping cohorts: the 610 includes every new ticket plus 86 older tickets.
- Evaluated an unreleased BERT candidate with 82.63% sealed-test accuracy and 0.7563 macro-F1.
- Measured the authenticated stored analytics-snapshot endpoint at 24.2 ms p50 and 45.8 ms p95 across 248 successful in-container requests; this is local warm-read evidence, not a production SLA, browser benchmark, or analytics-recomputation result.
- Reduced analytics visualization assets from about 1.07 MB to 415 KB raw and 361 KB to 123 KB gzip.
- Keeps external updates bounded by approval, lifecycle checks, and a checked-in hosted policy with automatic delivery disabled.

### Indian Parliamentary Data
- **Domain:** Research and Data Engineering
- **Tech:** Python, Selenium, SQLite, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Deepgram, PyMuPDF
- Multi-vendor speech and translation evaluation followed by a recoverable end-to-end pipeline for parliamentary records, campaign audio, and structured analysis data.
- Designed the evaluation phase at Studio Lab, then built the scraping, orchestration, extraction, normalization, and recovery logic under the Princeton appointment.

### SeeMyRace: Multimodal Race Photo Search
- **Domain:** Full-Stack Software Engineering and Applied ML
- **Tech:** Flask, PostgreSQL, pgvector, InsightFace/ArcFace, PaddleOCR, YOLOv8, Google Drive API, Docker
- Team-built full-stack application assembled primarily from open-source application, OCR, and data frameworks, with Google Drive as an external integration and separately licensed InsightFace `buffalo_l` research weights.
- Combines body-aware bib OCR with race-scoped ArcFace similarity search and an athlete-facing verification workflow.
- Vraj authored 32 commits on current main across 24 paths; the work landed through seven merged pull requests and included user-scoped match verification, GPX-backed race creation, admin and upload/search workflows, and OCR/SWT evaluation.
- The team replaced MongoDB-embedded float arrays with self-hosted PostgreSQL and pgvector for relational and vector data; it also evolved the face pipeline from 128-dimensional FaceNet/DeepFace embeddings to 512-dimensional ArcFace/InsightFace embeddings. These are architectural changes, not measured accuracy gains.
